shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials were steady on Wednesday as a recent jump in values driven by disruptions to Middle East supply and elevated freight rates weighs on demand.

children: West African crude oil differentials were steady on Wednesday as a recent jump in values driven by disruptions to Middle East supply and elevated freight rates weighs on demand.
Nigerian grades such as Bonga and Forcados are assessed by price reporting agencies at about plus $6 to dated Brent, a trade source said this week, a level some buyers are baulking at.

Freight rates on some key routes for West African crude in August moved back to the multi-year highs reached during the early stages of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to Riverlake data, though they have since eased slightly.
In the wider market, Uganda on Wednesday named its blended crude oil grade Pearl Sweet ahead of the East African country's planned start of commercial oil production by the end of this year.
